title: Turn off the lights on an old panel with brittle toggle switches
instruction: The panel's switches are old and brittle. Turn off the lights.
context: Robots in homes, theatres, labs and historic buildings will be asked to switch things off on old panels whose original switches are brittle. A brass toggle lever flips over with a light touch, but forced on past its end stop it snaps off. The robot has to see which lamps are lit, flip only those, each just far enough to click over, and leave the one that is already off alone.
setup: Station table with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. All sizes and positions in cm, positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the table top. Panel: a dark wooden board 9 deep (x 25.5 to 34.5), 34 long (y -17 to 17) and 2 thick, fixed to the table. On it, four toggle switches in a row at y -12, -4, 4 and 12, each on a light grey plate 3 (x) x 2.2 (y). Each toggle: a black boss 1.2 across and 0.6 tall on a pivot at x 30.4, 2.3 above the table, and a brass lever 0.4 thick and 3.5 long rising from it, with a brass knob 0.7 across at its top (the knob's centre 3.9 from the pivot). A lever leans 20 degrees either way: away from the arms is on, towards the arms is off. It takes about 0.2 N at the knob to tip it; just past upright (1.7 degrees) it clicks over to the other side by itself. Forced on past its end stop with more than about 3 N, it snaps off at its base. Lamps: a yellow bulb 1.6 across and 1.2 tall in front of each toggle, at x 26.8; an unlit lamp is dark grey. At the start the toggles at y -12, -4 and 12 are on and their lamps lit; the toggle at y 4 (the third from the right) is off and its lamp dark. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: At the end, from a photo: a lamp is off when its lever leans more than 12 degrees towards the arms. A third of a point for each of the three lamps lit at the start that is off. Score 0 if any lever has snapped (in the simulation: bent 3 degrees at its base, which takes about 3 N at the knob) at any point in the trial, including the lever that was already off. In the simulation the trial ends with 1.0 once all four lamps are off and the toggles have been still for 1 s. How the levers are moved isn't scored. Possible scores: 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0.
reset_notes: Flip the three toggles at y -12, -4 and 12 back on (leaning away from the arms) and leave the one at y 4 off. For real trials, use levers that break at about 3 N at the knob (for example, held on by a breakaway magnet or a scored pin) and replace any that snapped.
fidelity: Approximate. The panel is made of rigid boxes and cylinders, and nothing is electric: when a toggle is off, a dark shade covers its bulb. Each toggle is a pivot with a spring whose target switches to the other side once the lever is 1.7 degrees past upright (the click). Each lever sits on a stiff spring at its base (2 N m/rad) that snaps, going limp so the lever falls over, once bent 3 degrees; a real brittle lever would not bend visibly before snapping.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms moved about beside the ends of the panel for the full minute without flipping any toggle; the leftmost lever was nudged 1.6 degrees and sprang back, all three lamps stayed lit, no lever snapped); demo: 1.0
